title: Import and Export Under GST
outcomes: Apply GST on import of goods and services.
Determine export of goods and services.
Apply deemed exports, merchant exports and SEZ rules.

meta.exam_tip: For exports of services, test all five conditions in order.

concepts.title: Import of goods and services
body: Import of goods is an inter-State supply; IGST is levied under section 3(7) of the Customs Tariff Act at the time of import, on assessable value plus BCD and other duties (excluding IGST and compensation cess). The place of supply is the importer's location.

Import of services for consideration is a supply even outside business and attracts IGST under reverse charge in the recipient's hands (except OIDAR to non-taxable online recipients, where the foreign supplier pays). Import of services from related persons without consideration is a supply under Schedule I.
High-sea sales and in-bond sales from customs warehouses are not supplies (Schedule III); IGST is collected once at clearance for home consumption on the value including high-sea sale premium.
concepts.analogy: Imports are taxed at the border or under reverse charge.
concepts.work: IGST on imports of ₹10 lakh at 18% is ₹1,99,800 after BCD and SWS.

concepts.title: Export of goods and services
body: Export of goods is taking goods out of India (section 2(5) IGST). Export of services (section 2(6)) requires: supplier in India, recipient outside India, place of supply outside India, payment received in convertible foreign exchange or permitted INR, and the supplier and recipient not being mere establishments of one person.
Since 30 March 2026, intermediary services follow the recipient-location rule, so they can qualify as exports.
Exports are zero-rated: ITC is allowed even if the supply is exempt, and either refund of IGST paid or refund of unutilised ITC is available.
concepts.analogy: Five conditions make a service an export.
concepts.work: Consultancy to a US client paid in dollars is an export.

concepts.title: Zero-rated supplies and LUT
body: Section 16 IGST: zero-rated supply means export of goods or services and supplies to SEZ units or developers for authorised operations. The exporter may (a) export under bond or LUT without IGST and claim refund of unutilised ITC, or (b) pay IGST and claim refund (only notified persons or goods may use option (b) for goods).

Under LUT, goods must be exported within three months of the invoice and payment for services received within one year (extendable); otherwise tax is paid with interest within 15 days after those periods.
If export proceeds are not realised within the FEMA time limit, refund received must be repaid with interest within 30 days after expiry.
concepts.analogy: Zero-rated supplies are taxed at zero with credit retained.
concepts.work: Goods invoiced under LUT on 10 January must leave India by 10 April.

concepts.title: Deemed exports, merchant exports and SEZ
body: Deemed exports (section 147 CGST) are notified supplies of goods manufactured in India that do not leave India — supplies against Advance Authorisation, to EOUs, of capital goods against EPCG authorisation, and of gold by banks against Advance Authorisation. Tax is paid and refund can be claimed by recipient or supplier.
Supplies to registered merchant exporters are taxed at 0.1% (0.05% CGST + 0.05% SGST or 0.1% IGST), provided goods are exported within 90 days and other conditions are met.
Supplies to SEZ units/developers are inter-State and zero-rated for authorised operations; goods imported by SEZ units are exempt from IGST; supplies by SEZ units to the DTA are treated as imports.
concepts.analogy: Special regimes relieve tax on supplies linked to exports.
concepts.work: Goods worth ₹50 lakh to a merchant exporter carry only ₹5,000 of GST.

jobs.title: Export refund planning
jobs.situation: An exporter accumulates ITC every month.
steps: File LUT at the start of the year.
Track shipping bills and export within timelines.
jobs.takeaway: LUT preserves cash flow for regular exporters.

summary: Import of goods: IGST under CTA 3(7) on AV + duties.
Import of services: RCM; OIDAR exception.
Zero-rating: LUT or IGST refund; 3 months / 1 year.
remember: Branch abroad is not a separate person.
traps: Treating services to own foreign branch as exports.

viva.model: Exports of goods or services and supplies to SEZ units or developers for authorised operations.

viva.q: What are the two routes for zero-rated supplies?
viva.model: Supply under bond or LUT without IGST with refund of ITC, or pay IGST and claim refund.

viva.q: What happens if export proceeds are not realised?
viva.model: The refund must be repaid with interest within 30 days after the FEMA time limit.
Supplies to EOUs and supplies against Advance Authorisation.

viva.q: How are SEZ supplies into the DTA treated?
viva.model: As imports, attracting customs duty and IGST.

cases.title: Agastya Software
cases.case: Agastya Software (Bengaluru) provides development services to its wholly owned subsidiary in Singapore (a separate company) for USD 1,00,000, received in foreign exchange. It also provides services to its own branch in Dubai.

mcqs.q: Services to the Singapore subsidiary are:
mcqs.explain: Separate legal entity. In practice: all conditions met.

mcqs.q: Services to its own Dubai branch are:
options: Not an export — establishments of the same person
